item.content:encoded:
My tone was somewhat hostile; I was out of line. I saw this late at night, surrounded by a bunch of other mini-disasters, so I was rather on edge. My apologies, Roget.

Now, I know that the original is relatively new. I just considered it an exemplar of the old style. I can't write anything like the old 935, because I haven't anywhere near the skill. Besides, I can't really savor anything I myself wrote.

I do think it is too late to use the old canon. People have read the required reading, so it's all about hyper-clinical tone. Not one of the old greats would survive today. I wish I'd seen the discussion of 935. I knew it was dropping, but I thought it was stable for at least a while longer. I hadn't read 935 for a few weeks.

item.content:encoded:
I have no idea how to organize this post, so I'm gonna use bullets to list my thoughts.

  • I saw it at -14. If you want to blame anyone for it not being here any more, blame the readers.
  • The original version of this was created in late 2011 — it was just written in the old style. It's no more "one of our last links to the past" than any of the various ancient SCPs that managed to get by on being well-written.
  • You want something in the style of the old 935 on the wiki, do one of these things:
    • Write one yourself
    • Make a convincing argument that other people should attempt to do so, because it is NOT too late to use the old canon.
  • If you were really invested in the last version, it was dropping in rating for a while and Roget asked to do a rewrite two weeks ago. You could have offered to help him on it, or gotten in before him and just done it yourself.

For reference: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-400940 (I have no idea how long this link will last)

But most importantly: getting angry at someone who wanted to make an article acceptable to the wiki is rude. Especially when, if you'd gotten your way (and kept it the same), it would not be on the wiki AT ALL. So express your distaste for the present version, make your suggestions, and chillax.

item.content:encoded:
When a subject carrying Genetic Marker Bowe-1A reaches the age of 41, SCP-935 will teleport itself into their possession. Attempting to take it from the subject in the first 78 hours following its manifestation will result in its immediate return to the subject. All subjects who have possessed SCP-935 have have gone missing within 78 hours of coming into possession of it, with one exception. During its time in containment, approximately 6 subjects have been lost after coming into possession of SCP-935, and it is estimated that an additional 67 subjects were lost prior to initial containment.

After recovery, a card within SCP-935 will have detailed instructions on a specific card game to be played by the subject. These are always listed with the caveat that cheating will result in their demise. However, research into SCP-935 affected subjects show that they have all died within 78 hours of obtaining it, whether or not they completed the task. SCP-935 appears to make moves on its own, with cards being teleported into their positions as the game is played.

Could you clarify "recovery"? I'm not entirely clear on the chronology of events here.
